groups.title: Compute
groups.blurb: Where the code runs. The exam mostly asks which one costs least effort for the shape of the workload.

services.name: EC2
services.solves: A virtual machine you fully control: OS, agents, licences, GPUs.
use: Legacy or stateful apps that need the OS
Long-running work over 15 min or needing more than 10 GB RAM
Specific hardware: GPU, bare metal, BYOL per socket
services.avoid: Anything short, spiky and stateless that Lambda or Fargate would run with no servers to patch.

services.name: Lambda
services.solves: Run a function per event, pay per millisecond, nothing to manage.
use: Event-driven glue: S3 upload, SQS message, API call, schedule
Bursty traffic that would idle a server
Least operational overhead
services.avoid: Runs over 15 min, needs more than 10 GB, or needs a persistent connection or local state.

services.name: ECS on Fargate
services.solves: Run containers without managing instances.
use: Containerised app that outgrows Lambda limits
Predictable microservices where you do not want to patch hosts
Batch containers on Fargate Spot
services.avoid: You need GPUs, daemonsets or host-level control: use ECS on EC2 instead.

services.name: EKS
services.solves: Managed Kubernetes control plane.
use: Team already runs Kubernetes and wants to keep manifests and tooling
Multi-cloud or on-prem portability is a stated requirement
services.avoid: The question does not say Kubernetes. ECS is simpler and cheaper to run.

services.name: Elastic Beanstalk
services.solves: Deploy a web app from code; AWS provisions EC2, ALB, ASG and RDS for you.
use: Developers who want to upload code and not think about infrastructure
Standard web stacks: Java, .NET, Node, Python, Docker
services.avoid: You need control over the underlying resources. You still pay for what it creates.

services.name: AWS Batch
services.solves: Queue and run batch jobs on the cheapest compute, scaling to zero.
use: Thousands of jobs with dependencies, running on Spot
Jobs longer than Lambda's 15 min

comparisons.title: EC2 purchasing options
rows: None: you pay for the box
Socket or core BYOL licence, compliance
comparisons.verdict: Baseline on Reserved or a Savings Plan, burst on Spot, everything else On-Demand.

comparisons.title: Savings Plans vs Reserved Instances
rows: EC2 any family or Region, Fargate, Lambda
One family in one Region, any size
One instance type, Region or AZ
Mixed compute, may move to containers or Lambda
Never changing, want max discount, capacity reservation in an AZ
Need discount but expect to change type

comparisons.title: Lambda concurrency controls
rows: Caps how many concurrent executions this function may take from the account pool
One function starving the others, or throttling downstream
Limit blast radius, protect a database
Predictable latency, e.g. a checkout API

groups.title: Load balancing and scaling
groups.blurb: Which balancer, and how the fleet grows and shrinks.

services.name: Application Load Balancer
services.solves: Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS routing to targets across AZs.
use: Route by path, host, header, query string
Targets are EC2, ECS tasks, Lambda, or IPs including on-prem
Needs WAF, Cognito auth, sticky sessions, WebSocket
services.avoid: You need a static IP or non-HTTP protocols.

services.name: Network Load Balancer
services.solves: Layer 4 TCP/UDP/TLS at millions of requests per second with a static IP per AZ.
use: Partner needs to allowlist fixed IPs
Ultra-low latency, non-HTTP protocols
Preserve source IP to the target
Front an ALB when you need a static IP for HTTP

services.name: Gateway Load Balancer
services.solves: Transparently insert third-party appliances into the traffic path.
use: Firewall, IDS/IPS, deep packet inspection from a vendor
Uses GENEVE on port 6081 with an endpoint in each consumer VPC

services.name: Auto Scaling group
services.solves: Keep N healthy instances across AZs and change N on demand.
use: Replace unhealthy instances automatically
Scale on CPU, request count, queue depth, or a schedule
Mixed On-Demand and Spot in one group

comparisons.title: ALB vs NLB vs GWLB
rows: Yes, one Elastic IP per AZ
WAF, Cognito, Lambda targets, sticky sessions

comparisons.title: Auto Scaling policies
rows: Keep a metric at a value, e.g. CPU 50 %
You define one step and a cooldown
Needs at least 24 h of history
Cyclical traffic, want capacity ready before the spike
comparisons.verdict: Target tracking unless the question describes a schedule or a forecastable cycle.

comparisons.title: Health checks and lifecycle
rows: Your app answers on a path or port
Behind a load balancer, always enable
Copy logs before terminate, warm up before serving

groups.title: Storage
groups.blurb: Object, block or file. Then which tier inside each.

services.name: S3
services.solves: Unlimited object storage with 11 nines of durability and per-object tiering.
use: Static assets, backups, data lake, logs
Anything reached over HTTP rather than mounted
Lifecycle rules to move to cheaper tiers
services.avoid: A file system that many instances mount, or a database.

services.name: EBS
services.solves: A network block volume attached to one instance in one AZ.
use: Boot volumes, databases on EC2
Snapshots to S3 for backup and cross-AZ or cross-Region copy
Multi-Attach only for io1/io2 within one AZ with a cluster-aware file system
services.avoid: Shared access from many instances or across AZs.

services.name: Instance store
services.solves: Physically attached NVMe disk, highest IOPS, lost on stop or hardware failure.
use: Scratch, cache, buffer, replicated databases that tolerate loss
services.avoid: Anything that must survive a stop.

services.name: EFS
services.solves: POSIX NFS file system shared by thousands of Linux instances across AZs.
use: Shared content between web servers, home directories, CMS uploads
Lambda or containers needing a shared file system
Regional by default, One Zone for cheaper non-critical data

services.name: FSx for Windows File Server
services.solves: Managed SMB file share with NTFS, ACLs and Active Directory integration.
use: Windows workloads, lift-and-shift file servers, DFS namespaces

services.name: FSx for Lustre
services.solves: Parallel file system for HPC and ML with hundreds of GB/s.
use: Training or simulation over a dataset that lives in S3
Scratch for burst jobs, Persistent for long-running

services.name: FSx for NetApp ONTAP / OpenZFS
services.solves: Bring existing NetApp or ZFS features: multi-protocol, snapshots, cloning, dedup.
use: Migrating from NetApp; needs NFS and SMB and iSCSI on the same share
OpenZFS: NFS with low-latency snapshots, Linux only

services.name: Storage Gateway
services.solves: On-prem appliance that presents S3 as local storage with a cache.
use: S3 File Gateway: NFS/SMB share backed by S3
Volume Gateway: iSCSI block, cached or stored
Tape Gateway: replace a physical tape library with virtual tapes in Glacier

comparisons.title: EBS vs EFS vs FSx vs S3
rows: HPC, ML training on S3 data

comparisons.title: EBS volume types
rows: 3,000 baseline, up to 16,000, set independently of size
Critical databases needing more than 16k IOPS
comparisons.verdict: gp3 unless the number of IOPS says io2. HDD never boots.

comparisons.title: EFS storage classes and modes
rows: Lifecycle policy after N days without access
Accessed a few times a quarter
Accessed a few times a year

comparisons.title: S3 storage classes
rows: Unknown or changing pattern, no analysis
Archive needing instant read once a quarter
comparisons.verdict: "Unknown access pattern" is Intelligent-Tiering. "Milliseconds" rules out Flexible and Deep Archive.

comparisons.title: S3 access controls
rows: Grant another account, enforce TLS, restrict to a VPC endpoint
Almost never; disable with Object Ownership
Always on unless it is a public website
WORM: governance (overridable) or compliance (nobody, even root)

groups.title: Databases
groups.blurb: Relational vs NoSQL is the first cut. Then availability vs read scaling.

services.name: RDS
services.solves: Managed relational engines: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, Db2.
use: Existing SQL app, joins, transactions
Automated backups, patching, Multi-AZ with one checkbox
services.avoid: You need the OS, or a NoSQL access pattern at massive scale.

services.name: Aurora
services.solves: AWS-built MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible engine on a shared storage layer copied 6 ways across 3 AZs.
use: Higher performance and availability than RDS
Up to 15 readers on one endpoint, failover in about 30 s
Serverless v2 for variable or unknown load
Global Database for cross-Region under 1 s lag

services.name: DynamoDB
services.solves: Serverless key-value store with single-digit ms at any scale.
use: Session state, carts, profiles, IoT, leaderboards
Known access patterns by key
TTL to expire items, Streams to react to changes, Global Tables for active-active
services.avoid: Ad-hoc joins, complex queries across many attributes.

services.name: ElastiCache
services.solves: In-memory cache in front of a database, sub-ms reads.
use: Read-heavy relational workloads
Session store, leaderboards, pub/sub (Redis)

services.name: DAX
services.solves: Write-through cache built into DynamoDB, microsecond reads, no code change.
use: DynamoDB read hot spots
Question says microseconds and DynamoDB together

services.name: Redshift
services.solves: Petabyte columnar data warehouse for BI and complex joins.
use: OLAP, dashboards, joins across TBs
Spectrum to query S3 without loading
services.avoid: OLTP, or ad-hoc queries over S3 with nothing to provision: that is Athena.

services.name: Others to recognise
services.solves: Neptune is graphs. DocumentDB is MongoDB. Keyspaces is Cassandra. Timestream is time series. QLDB is an immutable ledger. MemoryDB is durable Redis as a primary database.
use: Pick by the word in the question

comparisons.title: RDS Multi-AZ vs read replica
rows: Read scaling, or a cross-Region copy
Same AZ, other AZ, or other Region
Taken from standby, no I/O pause
One extra per replica plus cross-Region transfer
Reporting, read-heavy, DR in another Region
comparisons.verdict: Sync and idle is availability. Async and readable is performance. A replica can also be Multi-AZ.

comparisons.title: Aurora options
rows: Read scaling and HA in one Region
Secondary promoted in under 1 min, RPO ~1 s
Up to 15, auto scaling, custom endpoints
Dev, test, unpredictable, pay per second
RPO under 1 s and RTO under 1 min across Regions

comparisons.title: Aurora vs RDS
rows: EBS, you pick size and type
Auto-grows to 128 TiB, 6 copies in 3 AZs
Up to 15 (5 on Oracle/SQL Server), async
Up to 15, share storage, ms lag
Higher base, better price per throughput
Oracle or SQL Server, or simple small DB

comparisons.title: DynamoDB capacity and indexes
rows: Index on any partition and sort key
Index with the same partition key, different sort key
Any time, switch once per 24 h
Unknown or spiky traffic, new tables
Alternate sort within one partition, strongly consistent

comparisons.title: ElastiCache Redis vs Memcached vs DAX
rows: Persistence, replication, Multi-AZ auto failover, backups
Multi-threaded, scales out by adding nodes
Anything that must survive, leaderboards, sessions
Simplest cache, large nodes, no HA needed
DynamoDB specifically, microseconds, no code change

groups.title: VPC and connectivity
groups.blurb: Traffic control inside the VPC, then getting out of it and connecting to others.

services.name: Security group
services.solves: Stateful firewall on an ENI: allow rules only, return traffic is automatic.
use: Default answer for instance-level control
Reference another SG as the source: 'only the ALB may talk to the app tier'

services.name: Network ACL
services.solves: Stateless subnet-level firewall with ordered allow and deny rules.
use: Block a specific IP or range
Defence in depth at subnet boundary
Remember ephemeral ports both ways

services.name: NAT Gateway
services.solves: Private subnet instances reach the internet for outbound only.
use: Patching, package downloads, calling public APIs from private instances
One per AZ for resilience, lives in a public subnet
IPv6 uses an egress-only internet gateway instead
services.avoid: Traffic to S3 or DynamoDB: use a gateway endpoint, it is free.

services.name: VPC endpoints
services.solves: Reach AWS services privately without an internet gateway or NAT.
use: Gateway endpoint: S3 and DynamoDB, free, a route table entry
Interface endpoint (PrivateLink): everything else, an ENI in your subnet, hourly cost
Endpoint policies to restrict which buckets or APIs

services.name: VPC peering
services.solves: Private routing between two VPCs, even across accounts and Regions.
use: A handful of VPCs
No overlapping CIDRs, not transitive
services.avoid: Many VPCs: the mesh explodes. Use Transit Gateway.

services.name: Transit Gateway
services.solves: Hub-and-spoke router for many VPCs, VPNs and Direct Connect.
use: Tens or hundreds of VPCs
Transitive routing, shared VPN or DX, multicast
Cross-Region peering of TGWs

services.name: PrivateLink
services.solves: Expose one service to other VPCs or accounts without peering or overlapping CIDR worries.
use: SaaS-style: consumers get an interface endpoint to your NLB
Only that service is reachable, nothing else in the VPC

services.name: Site-to-Site VPN
services.solves: Encrypted IPsec tunnel from on-prem over the public internet in minutes.
use: Quick, cheap hybrid link
Backup for Direct Connect
Accelerated VPN via Global Accelerator for jittery paths

services.name: Direct Connect
services.solves: Dedicated private fibre from your data centre to AWS.
use: Consistent latency, large sustained throughput, cheaper egress
Takes weeks to months; not encrypted by default, add VPN on top or MACsec
Two connections at two locations for resilience

services.name: Client VPN
services.solves: OpenVPN-based remote access for individual users into a VPC.
use: Remote staff needing private access
Auth via AD, SAML or certificates

comparisons.title: Security group vs network ACL
rows: Allow and deny, numbered, first match wins
Deny all inbound, allow all outbound
Default NACL allows all; custom denies all
Block a specific IP, subnet-wide deny

comparisons.title: Getting private subnets out
rows: Hourly per AZ plus per GB
Private subnet to S3, cut NAT cost
Private to any other AWS API, also from on-prem
comparisons.verdict: "Reduce NAT Gateway cost" plus S3 or DynamoDB equals gateway endpoint.

comparisons.title: Connecting VPCs and sites
rows: On-prem to VPC or many via DX Gateway

groups.title: Edge, DNS and acceleration
groups.blurb: Route 53 answers names, CloudFront caches, Global Accelerator routes over the backbone.

services.name: Route 53
services.solves: DNS with health checks and traffic-shaping routing policies.
use: Alias records to ALB, CloudFront, S3 website at the zone apex
Failover, latency, geolocation, weighted, multivalue routing
Private hosted zones for VPC-internal names

services.name: CloudFront
services.solves: CDN that caches HTTP content at edge locations worldwide.
use: Static and dynamic web content, video, APIs
Origin Access Control to keep S3 private
Signed URLs or cookies for paid content
Lambda@Edge and CloudFront Functions to rewrite requests
Field-level encryption, WAF and Shield attach here

services.name: Global Accelerator
services.solves: Two static anycast IPs that route any TCP/UDP traffic over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint.
use: Gaming, VoIP, IoT, non-HTTP
Static IPs for allowlisting in front of ALB/NLB/EIP
Fast cross-Region failover, deterministic routing
services.avoid: Caching. It does not cache anything.

services.name: S3 Transfer Acceleration
services.solves: Upload to a far-away bucket faster by entering at the nearest edge and riding the backbone.
use: Global users uploading large files to one bucket
Pair with multipart upload for anything over 100 MB

comparisons.title: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator vs Transfer Acceleration
rows: Cache content close to users, S3 websites, video
Non-HTTP, static IP, gaming, fast Regional failover
Users far from the bucket uploading large objects

comparisons.title: Route 53 routing policies
rows: Shift traffic between Regions on purpose
comparisons.verdict: "Fastest" is latency. "Must stay in country" is geolocation. "Standby" is failover.

groups.title: Identity and security
groups.blurb: Who can do what, where the guard rails sit, and which service watches which layer.

services.name: IAM
services.solves: Users, groups, roles and policies inside one account.
use: Roles for anything running on AWS, never long-lived keys
Identity policies grant, resource policies grant cross-account, permission boundaries cap
Explicit deny always wins

services.name: Organizations and SCPs
services.solves: Many accounts under one payer with guard rails that even root cannot bypass.
use: Consolidated billing and shared Reserved discounts
SCPs to deny a Region, a service, or disabling CloudTrail
OUs for prod vs sandbox
services.avoid: SCPs do not grant anything and do not apply to the management account.

services.name: IAM Identity Center
services.solves: Single sign-on to many accounts and SaaS apps from one identity source.
use: Workforce SSO with AD or Okta
Permission sets across an Organization

services.name: Cognito
services.solves: Sign-up, sign-in and tokens for your own app's customers.
use: User pool: directory and JWTs, social login, MFA
Identity pool: swap a token for temporary AWS credentials, guest access

services.name: Directory Service
services.solves: Active Directory in AWS, in three flavours.
use: See the comparison below; the exam asks which flavour

services.name: KMS
services.solves: Managed keys for envelope encryption across almost every service.
use: Customer managed keys for audit, rotation and cross-account grants
Multi-Region keys for replicated data
4 KB limit per direct encrypt call

services.name: CloudHSM
services.solves: Single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 hardware you control.
use: Regulatory need to own the key material
Oracle TDE, SSL offload, custom key store for KMS

services.name: Secrets Manager
services.solves: Store and automatically rotate database and API credentials.
use: RDS, Redshift, DocumentDB rotation with a Lambda
Cross-account secret sharing
services.avoid: Plain config values: Parameter Store standard tier is free.

services.name: ACM
services.solves: Free public TLS certificates with auto-renewal for ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway.
use: CloudFront certs must live in us-east-1
Private CA for internal certs

services.name: WAF
services.solves: Layer 7 rules on ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito.
use: SQL injection, XSS, geo block, rate limit per IP, bot control
Managed rule groups from AWS and vendors

services.name: Shield
services.solves: DDoS protection. Standard is free and on; Advanced adds 24/7 response, cost protection, and WAF at no charge.
use: Advanced when the question mentions sophisticated DDoS, cost of scaling during an attack, or the DRT

services.name: GuardDuty
services.solves: Threat detection from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, EKS, S3, Malware.
use: Compromised credentials, crypto mining, unusual API calls
Nothing to install; findings go to EventBridge

services.name: Inspector
services.solves: Vulnerability scanning of EC2, container images and Lambda.
use: CVEs and network reachability
Continuous, agent via SSM

services.name: Macie
services.solves: Finds PII and sensitive data in S3 with ML.
use: Question says S3 and personal data or compliance discovery

services.name: Security Hub and Detective
services.solves: Security Hub aggregates findings and scores against standards. Detective builds a graph to investigate a finding's root cause.
use: Single pane across accounts
Detective when the question says investigate or root cause

services.name: Network Firewall
services.solves: Managed stateful firewall at the VPC level with domain, IP and Suricata rules.
use: Central egress filtering, intrusion prevention across VPCs
Deployed via Firewall Manager for the whole Organization

comparisons.title: Policy types
rows: Let another account in, or restrict a resource
Guard rail: no Region X, no leaving the org
comparisons.verdict: Effective = (identity OR resource) AND boundary AND SCP AND session, minus any explicit deny.

comparisons.title: Directory Service flavours
rows: Real Windows AD running in AWS, Multi-AZ
A proxy to your on-prem AD, nothing stored
In AWS, plus trust to on-prem
FSx Windows, RDS SQL Server, SSO, EC2 domain join, MFA via RADIUS
EC2 domain join, SSO, WorkSpaces, MFA
Small: under 5,000 users, no MFA, no trust
Need AD in AWS, or hybrid with a trust, or AD-aware services
Keep everything on-prem, just let AWS authenticate against it
Cheap, small, Linux-friendly, no Microsoft features

comparisons.title: S3 encryption options
rows: KMS request quota, Bucket Keys reduce it
HTTPS mandatory, you lose key you lose data
Need control or audit of the key

comparisons.title: Which security service watches what
rows: Is this bucket public, was it always

comparisons.title: WAF vs Shield vs Network Firewall vs NACL
rows: SQLi, XSS, bots, rate abuse, geo
DDoS with SLA and money back
Central inspection of all VPC traffic

groups.title: Messaging and integration
groups.blurb: Decoupling. The words 'lose', 'order', 'replay' and 'fan out' each point to one service.

services.name: SQS
services.solves: Durable queue that buffers work between producers and consumers.
use: Absorb spikes, never lose a request, retry with a dead-letter queue
Consumers scale on queue depth
Long polling to cut cost, visibility timeout to avoid double work

services.name: SNS
services.solves: Push one message to many subscribers at once.
use: Fan out to SQS queues, Lambda, HTTP, email, SMS
Message filtering per subscription
Alarms and notifications

services.name: EventBridge
services.solves: Event bus that routes by content from AWS services, SaaS and your apps.
use: React to an AWS event: instance stopped, object created
Rules with content filters, schema registry, archive and replay
Scheduler for cron

services.name: Step Functions
services.solves: Orchestrate multi-step workflows with retries, branching and waits.
use: Lambda chains getting unwieldy
Human approval, long waits up to a year (Standard)
Express for high-volume short workflows

services.name: Amazon MQ
services.solves: Managed ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ for apps that already speak JMS, AMQP, MQTT, STOMP.
use: Lift and shift a broker without rewriting
services.avoid: New apps: use SQS/SNS, they scale better.

services.name: API Gateway
services.solves: Managed front door for REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs.
use: Throttling, usage plans and API keys, caching, auth via Cognito, IAM or Lambda authorizer
Lambda or any HTTP backend, private via VPC link
WebSocket for two-way

services.name: AppSync
services.solves: Managed GraphQL with real-time subscriptions and offline sync.
use: Question says GraphQL, or mobile app with real-time updates

comparisons.title: SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge
rows: By any field in the event
React to AWS events, route by content, schedule
comparisons.verdict: Fan out plus durability is SNS in front of one SQS queue per consumer.

comparisons.title: SQS Standard vs FIFO
rows: Exactly once, dedup by id or content hash in 5 min
300 msg/s, 3,000 with batching, higher in high-throughput mode
Order matters, no duplicates: payments, inventory

comparisons.title: Kinesis Data Streams vs Firehose vs SQS vs MSK
rows: Load a stream into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, HTTP
Near real time, 60 s or 1 MB buffer
Lambda inline, format conversion to Parquet
Clickstream, IoT, multiple apps reading the same stream
Simplest path stream to S3, zero code
comparisons.verdict: "Replay" or "multiple consumers" is Streams. "Deliver to S3 with least effort" is Firehose.

comparisons.title: API Gateway flavours and Lambda invocation
rows: Usage plans, API keys, caching, WAF, request validation, private
Just HTTPS in, IAM or none auth
Need throttling per client, caching, or private endpoint
Lambda mixed with EC2 behind one ALB

comparisons.title: Step Functions Standard vs Express
rows: At least once, logs to CloudWatch
High volume, short: IoT ingestion, streaming transforms

groups.title: Analytics and data movement
groups.blurb: Query it where it lies, or move it. Each service maps to one verb.

services.name: Athena
services.solves: SQL over files in S3, serverless, pay per TB scanned.
use: Ad-hoc queries on logs or a data lake
Cut cost with Parquet, partitions and compression
Glue Data Catalog holds the schema

services.name: Glue
services.solves: Serverless ETL and the data catalog.
use: Crawlers to discover schemas
Spark jobs to convert CSV to Parquet
Glue DataBrew for no-code cleaning

services.name: EMR
services.solves: Managed Hadoop, Spark, Hive, Presto clusters.
use: Existing Spark jobs, big custom processing
Task nodes on Spot for cost

services.name: OpenSearch
services.solves: Full-text search and log analytics with dashboards.
use: Search a catalogue, analyse logs, Kibana-style dashboards
Common target from Firehose

services.name: QuickSight
services.solves: Serverless BI dashboards with SPICE in-memory engine.
use: Business dashboards over Redshift, Athena, RDS, S3

services.name: DataSync
services.solves: Fast online transfer of files between on-prem NFS/SMB and S3, EFS or FSx, on a schedule.
use: Migrate or continuously sync a file share
Preserves metadata, verifies data

services.name: DMS
services.solves: Migrate databases with the source running, homogeneous or heterogeneous.
use: Continuous replication with CDC
Schema Conversion Tool for Oracle to Aurora

services.name: Snow family
services.solves: Physical devices for moving tens of TB to PB when the network is too slow.
use: Snowcone 8 TB, Snowball Edge 80 TB, edge compute
Rule of thumb: over a week to transfer online, ship it

services.name: Transfer Family
services.solves: Managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP, AS2 endpoint in front of S3 or EFS.
use: Partners must keep using SFTP

comparisons.title: Athena vs Redshift vs EMR vs OpenSearch
rows: Query logs once in a while

comparisons.title: Moving data in
rows: Migrate NFS/SMB to S3, EFS, FSx
Too much data for the link, or no link

groups.title: Observability, governance and DR
groups.blurb: What happened, who did it, what does it look like now, and how fast can you come back.

services.name: CloudWatch
services.solves: Metrics, logs, alarms and dashboards.
use: Alarm on a metric, scale or notify
Logs Insights to query logs, metric filters to alarm on log patterns
Custom metrics and the agent for memory and disk

services.name: CloudTrail
services.solves: Records every API call: who, when, from where.
use: Audit, compliance, 'who deleted the bucket'
Organization trail to S3 with log file validation
Data events for S3 object-level and Lambda invocations

services.name: AWS Config
services.solves: Records resource configuration over time and evaluates rules.
use: Is every EBS volume encrypted, and when did that bucket become public
Auto-remediate with SSM documents
Conformance packs across the Organization

services.name: X-Ray
services.solves: Distributed tracing of one request across services.
use: Find where latency goes in a microservice chain

services.name: Systems Manager
services.solves: Fleet operations without SSH: run commands, patch, sessions, parameters.
use: Session Manager instead of bastions and port 22
Patch Manager, Run Command, State Manager
Parameter Store for config

services.name: Trusted Advisor
services.solves: Checks cost, performance, security, fault tolerance and service limits against best practice.
use: Full checks need Business or Enterprise support

services.name: Control Tower
services.solves: Landing zone: set up a multi-account Organization with guard rails in a few clicks.
use: New Organization, account factory, preventive (SCP) and detective (Config) guard rails

services.name: AWS Backup
services.solves: Central backup policies across EBS, RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3 and more.
use: One policy, cross-Region and cross-account copies, vault lock for WORM

services.name: Elastic Disaster Recovery
services.solves: Continuous block-level replication of servers to a cheap staging area, recover in minutes.
use: Lift-and-shift DR for on-prem or EC2 with low RPO and RTO

comparisons.title: CloudWatch vs CloudTrail vs Config vs X-Ray
rows: What does it look like and did it change
Where did this request spend time

comparisons.title: Disaster recovery strategies
rows: Database must be current, app can boot
Must serve some load immediately, scale up on failover
comparisons.verdict: Pilot light: data on, compute off. Warm standby: everything on, small.

comparisons.title: Cost tools
rows: Alert when spend or usage crosses a threshold
Most detailed line items to S3
Prevent a surprise bill, actions on breach
